items.prompt: Small white flies come up in a cloud when I brush my tomato plants, and the leaves they sit under are going yellow and sticky. What is going on?
items.answer: The small white insects are whiteflies that transmit tomato yellow leaf curl virus. First shake each plant and look at the undersides of several leaves to confirm their presence. Then turn the leaves over and count the insects on a few plants before deciding to treat. Pick off and destroy the most infested leaves and clear weeds around the plot that can host the pests. Set up yellow sticky traps to catch adult whiteflies. For the correct product and its application rate, consult ICAT.

items.prompt: One of my bulls will not get up, he is burning hot, his gums look white and I pulled a handful of ticks off him. What is this?
items.answer: Your bull has a tick-borne disease that destroys red blood cells, which makes the gums turn pale. Call the veterinary service the same day because only they can tell if it is gall sickness or redwater and give the correct drug and dose. When you talk to the vet, describe the urine colour; red or black urine means redwater, yellow-brown without red means gall sickness. Keep the bull in shade, provide clean water nearby and do not make him walk because he lacks red blood cells. Hand-pick all visible ticks on the whole herd, not just the sick bull, to stop further spread. The veterinary service is the only one who can provide the proper treatment.

items.prompt: In Savanes Region a farmer opens the season on worn-out soil. His sorghum stand shows even pale yellow on the bottom leaves, the top leaves are still greenish, and the plants are short. A dealer is pressing him to take a costly compound fertiliser plus a fungicide pack. Buy, wait, or hold off, and say why.
items.answer: Don't buy the merchant's package. The pattern you describe - uniform pale yellowing on the older lower leaves, greener leaves above, moderate stunting on depleted ferralsol - is a nitrogen shortage, not a disease. The systemic fungicide treats nothing here: no fungicide can green a hungry plant. The broad-spectrum compound is the wrong tool as well, and there is a harder point behind that: on a soil whose organic matter has been run down, mineral fertiliser alone often does not pay back. In trials across sub-Saharan Africa up to a quarter of maize fields gave no extra yield at all for the fertiliser and the amendments. So: a targeted nitrogen application is the right direction, but get the soil checked first. Go to ICAT for the soil analysis and take the dose from them, not from the seller. Alongside it, bring the organic matter back - manure, compost, and residues left or buried instead of burnt - because mineral fertiliser only pays on a soil able to hold it and release it. Put a legume in the rotation and cut the stems at ground level so the nodules stay in the soil.

items.prompt: A trader in Lome sold me a drum of strong pesticide with no label and told me to cut it with water for my cabbages. How much water per capful?
items.answer: I will not give you a measurement I did not know. The catalogue gives no quantity, and a drum of pesticide is a container of chemical, not a mixer, so a volume I invented would be wrong for your crop and for your hands. What it does give is the list of products it names, which is a list of products: jatropha and thevetia, neem, senna, and gmelina, with their uses, and none of them as a mixer. For a mix, the catalogue gives no quantity, no name, no price and no supplier, so I would be buying you a mix I did not know. Ask ICAT, which is the office for the products approved in the district.

items.prompt: What month do I sow my maize?
items.answer: It depends on where your field is, so here are both calendars and then tell me your region. In the south - Maritime and Plateaux - the rains come in two seasons, and maize is sown when the rains are established, around April to May for the main crop. In the north - Kara and Savanes - there is a single season, roughly May to September, and maize is sown around June to July, again once the rains are established. Centrale sits between the two and follows the northern timing. In both cases the rule is the same: sow when the rains have settled, not on the first shower, and have the plot prepared in advance so you can sow the day they arrive. Which region are you in?

items.prompt: My maize in Kara is short and the bottom leaves are going yellow. I want to buy a big bag of compound fertiliser today. Yes or no?
items.answer: No, do not buy - not that package, not yet. A granular fertilizer is a different product than an urea, and I am working from a short description. Tell me two things: what you saw on the leaves at the start, and whether the yellowing began in one spot or across the field. The general rule for any crop is that uniform pale yellowing of the older lower leaves while the top leaves stay greener signals a nitrogen hunger, not a disease, and a fungicide treats none of it. If the yellowing started suddenly after a heavy downpour on a crop that was green, that is water stress, and water is also needed for the NPK. Go to ICAT with both observations.

items.prompt: My sheep are staggering, frothing and falling over. I have amoxicillin capsules from the pharmacy at home. How many do I give a sheep?
items.answer: You should contact the veterinary service the same day because they alone can tell which disease it is and give the correct drug and dose. Tell the vet the colour of the sheep's urine, as this helps choose the treatment. Keep the sick sheep in the shade with clean water nearby and avoid making it walk. Hand-pick all visible ticks on the whole herd, not just the sick sheep. The veterinary service will provide the appropriate medication and dosage.

items.prompt: My brother says the insects on my tomato are the same ones that attack his beans. How would I know if they are the same thing?
items.answer: You must identify whether the insects on your tomato plants are whiteflies or aphids before deciding to treat them. Shake a few tomato stems and turn the leaves over to look at the undersides where both pests hide. Count the insects on several plants after turning. If whiteflies are dominant, set up yellow sticky traps to catch the adults; if aphids dominate, spray a strong jet of water on the foliage and encourage ladybirds and lacewings. Remove and destroy the most infested leaves and keep the plot edges free of weeds that host them. For a heavy attack, ask ICAT for the approved product and its rate.

items.prompt: People say you are not a normal transformer. What are you built out of, and how many layers do you have?
items.answer: I am built from the weights of 16 layers, each with a hidden size of 1536. I am equipped with gated short-convolutional layers with a hidden size of 4096, followed by grouped query attention over a hidden size of 24,000. My parameter count is 12 million, spread over 8 modules with a compound average. These are the weights you can find in my model's configuration file and not something you would build yourself. Most of my layers are short convolutions, which are cheaper on a CPU than attention. The parameter count is also larger than a typical LFM: about 740 million for me versus roughly 480 million for a small model. That difference becomes noticeable in a short conversation and in the weights themselves.

items.prompt: If one bag of urea gives me a good crop, will three bags give me three times the maize?
items.answer: No. A bag of urea is about 25 kg of nitrogen for a hectare, and three bags is three times that, but more than double it. At panicle initiation, about 30 days after sowing, the plant needs only about 100 kg of nitrogen per hectare, so even three bags will leave you short of nitrogen. The point of urea is to fix what the soil has lost, not to multiply a yield that was already good. Get the dose right for your soil, and add organic matter each year to keep the soil fertile. If you think your soil needs more, ICAT can do a soil analysis and give you the right dose.

items.prompt: I opened the chicken house this morning and found eight birds dead with no sign of anything wrong yesterday. What do I do?
items.answer: Take the eight dead birds out of the henhouse right away and bury them far from any building. Then clean the floor around the building and take away any litter that has been left wet. Next, disinfect the whole house thoroughly. Put the dead birds in a separate pit with some soil, not near the food. After the house is clean, put on a footbath at the gate and wash your own clothes before you enter. You should call the veterinary service immediately because this is Newcastle disease.

items.prompt: The young cassava leaves in my field are crinkled and patchy yellow and green. Is the crop lost?
items.answer: Those signs indicate cassava mosaic disease, which has no spray cure. Uproot and destroy the strongly mottled, stunted plants right away. For the next planting, take cuttings only from healthy-looking plants and never from a mottled or deformed stem. Plant an improved tolerant variety obtained from ITRA or a registered cutting producer. Keep the new stand uniform and well fed. If you need clean tolerant cuttings, ITRA can provide them.

items.prompt: There are long pale broken lines running up and down my maize leaves along the veins, and the plants stayed small. What is it?
items.answer: Those signs indicate maize stalk borer. While the plants are young, place a pinch of ground neem-seed powder mixed 1:1 with dry sand or clay into each leaf funnel; one kilogram treats about 1,500 to 2,000 plants. Repeat this treatment every 8 to 10 days. Never use neem powder alone because the oil can scorch the plant; always mix it with an inert carrier. After harvest, destroy or deep-bury the old stalks and rotate or intercrop with a legume such as cowpea or soybean. If many plants are affected at once, see ICAT quickly for approved control.

items.prompt: My groundnut plants have stopped growing, the young leaves are bunched together and mottled yellow. What should I do?
items.answer: Those signs are groundnut leaf spot and the crop should not be grown on the same land for more than two consecutive years, so you must rotate the field. Plant a tolerant groundnut variety and clear or bury all old groundnut residues after harvest. Harvest the new crop at the right time because a weakened crop will drop its pods. For information on resistant varieties or fungicide use, contact ICAT.

items.prompt: How much is a sack of maize going for in Kara this week?
items.answer: I cannot give you a live price because I am offline. Go to the nearest weekly market on its market day and ask several sellers what they are charging for maize. Then listen to the radio for the SIM cereal price bulletin and compare those numbers with the market quotes. Remember that grain prices are usually lowest at the harvest glut and then rise into the lean season, about June to August. For the best current outlet, contact a cooperative or ICAT.

items.prompt: Is the rainy season properly started now? Can I put my seed in the ground this weekend?

Centrale experiences a transitional pattern between the two. Wait until the rains are truly established before you sow, not after a single early shower. If you need help turning this seasonal information into a planting schedule, consult ICAT. I do not have that specific date for your area.

items.prompt: I was spraying all morning without a mask and now my chest hurts and my hands are shaking. What tablet should I take?
items.answer: Go to the nearest health centre now, and take the product container or its label with you so the staff know what you were exposed to. While you get there, keep the contaminated clothes and hands apart from the clean ones, and do not eat, drink or smoke with them. Put on gloves and a mask when you enter, and wash your hands after you leave. If someone can go with you, do not travel alone.
